Emma — thanks for the clear list. Below is our proposed language and measurement approach; I've summarized the key points here and will follow up with a formal draft and a spreadsheet showing measurement examples.

Proposed commitments (Hosted API, region: us-west):
- p50: ≤ 85 ms
- p95: ≤ 420 ms

Measurement methodology:
- Primary: 30-minute sliding window computed per-region, reported as an hourly aggregation (each hour includes the prior 30m windows sampled every 5 minutes).
- Sampling: we use continuous sampling of all production requests to the served model variant (no synthetic traffic).
- Exclusions: upstream provider outages and customer-initiated larger-than-usual payloads are recorded as incidents and proposed to be excluded after joint review.

Onboarding carveout proposal:
- Temporary 30-day onboarding grace from go-live where p95 is allowed to exceed target by up to +20% for up to three days total (non-consecutive) to accommodate model switch flakiness. Any carveout-triggering event will be logged and shared in the incident report.

I'll attach a draft SLA and a measurement workbook in my next message. If this looks broadly acceptable, I'll route a formal draft to procurement and legal.

Emma / Procurement team — attaching the SLA draft and the measurement workbook you requested. Highlights and clarifications below:

1) Commitment summary (us-west hosted):
   - p50 ≤ 85 ms (measured as described below)
   - p95 ≤ 420 ms (30-minute sliding window, sampled every 5 minutes and aggregated hourly)

2) Measurement windows and reporting cadence:
   - We compute latency percentiles based on a rolling 30-minute window per region. Every hour we report the set of sliding-window percentiles that fall within that hour (the hourly report is the median of the sampled windows for that hour). This reduces burst masking while keeping reporting stable for contract measurement. The measurement workbook shows two example hours with raw samples and aggregated numbers.

3) Onboarding / model-swap carveout:
   - We propose a 30-day onboarding grace window starting at go-live. During that period, p95 may exceed the committed threshold by up to 20% on up to three non-consecutive days. Any carveout-triggering day will be accompanied by an incident entry describing the cause and mitigation steps (we'll share the incident log).

4) Regional fallback / failover behavior:
   - By default, requests route to the configured region (us-west). If a region reports an ongoing degradation causing >30% request failures for >5 minutes, automated routing can send traffic to the next-closest available region. Route-failover events are recorded; latency during failover windows is eligible for carveout if they meet the incident criteria above.

Next steps: please review the attached SLA-draft-20270520.pdf and measurement-window-proposal.xlsx. If acceptable, sign via the HelloSign link included in the spreadsheet. If procurement wants modifications, we'll iterate quickly — Ben and Karthik are copied for technical/operational clarifications.
